en: The picture on the package was apparently modeled after the chairman of the company.
Flavorsome yellow bean jam inside plump pastry. It has a mellow taste and isn't sickeningly sweet.
Tsurunoko has been a popular confection in Hakata since it was first made in 1905.
Hakata Niwaka is a traditional folk art familiar to all Hakata residents.
Niwaka Senbei are amusing treats made in the shape of the half-masks used in the art.
Made with a generous amount of the finest flour and eggs and baked a golden brown, they are famous for their crunchy texture and egg flavor.
Each box contains a mask, reflecting the playful spirit of Hakata's people.
A local specialty made by Hanamidori, one of Hakata's most famous mizutaki restaurants.
This handmade treat is full of their house brand spicy fish roe and is a perfect accompaniment to any meal or drink.
A new favorite that combines potato chips and chocolate.
The light and crunchy potato chips are cut extra thin and coated with a layer of chocolate on one side that retains the potato aroma.
Sweet chocolate and salty potato chips blend together into a perfect harmony.
Cat tongue cookies are baked just long enough to add a golden tinge to the edges of the white cookie.
To get just the right result, the oven temperature must be monitored carefully.
The white chocolate sandwiched between the cookie halves is a blend created specially for Shiroi Koibito.
The sweet, smooth chocolate in the center adds the final touch to the Shiroi Koibito cookie, which has been a favorite for over thirty years.
Nature's finest, golden-yellow corn coated with high quality white chocolate.
One bite is enough to convey that this treat is a labor of love with nature's blessings from the fields of the north.
Particular attention is paid to preserving the original flavor of the ingredients.
This handmade delicacy is the result of a painstaking effort to do justice to nature's wonders.
Sapporo Agricultural College, a predecessor to Hokkaido University, was founded in 1876. Its teachers included Dr. William S. Clark.
It produced much talent based on the philosophies of frontier spirit, global perspective, all-round education, and practical learning.
This luxurious cookie includes generous amounts of Hokkaido milk. Its light, melt-in-your-mouth texture is enjoyed across Japan.
Sapporo Curry Yoshimi, known for Sapporo's famous soup curries, created this novel take on the rice cracker with a great flavor and aroma.
The chef's original spicy garam masala seals the deal, along with the aromatic shrimp baked into the senbei cracker.
They recreate an authentic soup curry taste.
Direct from the factory in Hokkaido to you! Individually wrapped crackers you can enjoy whenever you like.
A snack that replicates the taste of Sekai no Yamachan's premium chicken wings.
Their moist texture and aromatic fragrance make it hard to stop eating once you start.
You can recreate the taste of Yamamotoya Honten at home easily by simply boiling this in water.
Enjoy the delicious taste of freshly cooked noodles.
The aromatic Azuki Tsubu-an is made from meticulously steamed Hokkaido red beans.
The light-tasting Matcha-an is made with local Aichi Prefecture green tea, resulting in a mellow taste.
The Beni Tsubu-an is a colorful confection with white azuki beans.
Edo period traditions and skills are behind the flavorsome taste of this treat, which is made with carefully cooked fresh shrimp.
The manufacturer contacts producers directly to select only the best ingredients, and the manufacturing process locks the freshness in.
This confection lets you sample the taste of nature.
These rice cakes are made with non-glutinous rice flour, giving them a springy yet firm feel. Much effort has been put into their refined flavor.
They have a simple, elegant texture and feature five sweet-smelling flavors.
White tea, black tea, green tea, freshly steeped tea, and cherry blossom.
A juicy fried squid topped off with Kushikatsu Daruma's one-dip only sauce.
The subtle fragrance of the sauce and the delicious squid make this a real delicacy.
Osaka's famous 551 Horai Pork Buns are each lovingly shaped by expert chefs.
The pork is of course the star of the show, and it is diced instead of minced to produce a better texture.
The sweet onion and juicy pork create a taste sensation in your mouth!
The other key point is the bun, which has a slight sweetness to bring out the flavor of the other ingredients.
These takoyaki contain choice ingredients and are cooked by hand on a special copper plate using bamboo chopsticks.
Most Osaka residents can even sing the commercial's jingle. Takomasa's takoyaki is pretty much Osaka's most famous specialty food.
Tsuruhashi Fugetsu's okonomiyaki is a healthy and addictive traditional treat.
All the sauce and other toppings are inside, so you can just heat it up in the microwave when you want to enjoy the authentic taste.
Each one is cooked by hand, so the taste is identical to what you can enjoy at the restaurant itself.
Osaka's famous okonomiyaki in cracker form. This snack features the strong taste of dried bonito and sauce, and it goes well with beer.
Packaged in bite-sized pieces, they can be enjoyed anywhere easily.

In Shinada's Side Story "The Cost of a Swing," Shinada can change his baseball equipment.
There are three kinds of equipment that can be changed: bats, gloves, and cleats. You can change them by speaking to the clerk at the batting center.
Initially, Shinada uses cheap equipment. Better equipment can be bought at the pawn shop or elsewhere and equipped at the batting center to improve Shinada's batting skills.
